en: Proverbs 26

p.src: 1  Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.

en: Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
u.src: 1  Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.

p.src: 2  Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.

en: Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.
u.src: 2  Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.

p.src: 3  A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!

en: A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!
u.src: 3  A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!

p.src: 4  Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.

en: Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.
u.src: 4  Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.

p.src: 5  Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.

en: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.
u.src: 5  Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.

p.src: 6  One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.

en: One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.
u.src: 6  One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.

p.src: 7  Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

en: Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
u.src: 7  Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

p.src: 8  As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.

en: As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.
u.src: 8  As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.

p.src: 9  Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

en: Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
u.src: 9  Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

p.src: 10  As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.

en: As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.
u.src: 10  As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.

p.src: 11  As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.

en: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.
u.src: 11  As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.

p.src: 12  Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

en: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
u.src: 12  Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

p.src: 13  The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”

en: The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”
u.src: 13  The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”

p.src: 14  As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.

en: As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.
u.src: 14  As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.

p.src: 15  The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.

en: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
u.src: 15  The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.

p.src: 16  The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.

en: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.
u.src: 16  The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.

p.src: 17  Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.

en: Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.
u.src: 17  Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.

p.src: 18  Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death, 19  is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”

zh: 人欺凌鄰舍，卻說： 我豈不是戲耍嗎？ 他就像瘋狂的人拋擲火把、利箭， 與殺人的兵器。
en: Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,
is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”
u.src: 18  Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death, 19  is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”

p.src: 20  For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.

en: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
u.src: 20  For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.

p.src: 21  As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.

en: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.
u.src: 21  As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.

p.src: 22  The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.

en: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.
u.src: 22  The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.

p.src: 23  Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.

en: Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.
u.src: 23  Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.

p.src: 24  A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.

en: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.
u.src: 24  A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.

p.src: 25  When his speech is charming, don’t believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.

en: When his speech is charming, don’t believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.
u.src: 25  When his speech is charming, don’t believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.

p.src: 26  His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

en: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
u.src: 26  His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

p.src: 27  Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.

en: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
u.src: 27  Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.

p.src: 28  A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.

en: A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.
u.src: 28  A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.
